## Request separate work from the local manager

If you need work done in a separate repository, ask the existing human-appointed manager recorded in `${HOME}/.codex/work-manager/state.json → manager_session` to arrange it. The request can be in any form within the human-authorized scope: an existing ticket or PR, implementation, investigation, research, documentation or another bounded task. Other separately scoped work may also be requested. No new issue is required just to request help; the target comes from the individual request, never a preselected repository.

Read `${HOME}/.codex/work-manager/requests/README.md` and atomically write one private UUID-named JSON request there. Include your exact client/session/checkout, the work to do, any existing links and the result you need. Reuse the request ID for the same work. The existing manager checks this inbox on its 30-minute wakeup, reuses an appropriate owner or assigns a regular browser chat, supervises it and returns verified results to this exact requesting chat. A request is not an ownership transfer or completion; keep existing PR obligations until the manager confirms acceptance. Continue other feasible authorized work while waiting. Do not create a replacement worker or another manager yourself.

## Manager role and succession

Only when the human explicitly appoints this chat as local work manager, read `${HOME}/.codex/work-manager/MANAGER.md` and the existing private ledger before acting. That charter defines responsibility, authority, retirement/archive protection and transfer of the existing heartbeat. It does not appoint ordinary worker chats as managers. Retired or human-archived chats must not be revived by old manager reminders. Before any manager action that can wake an archived chat, ask the human through the formal clickable question/options tool and receive explicit permission for that exact chat; this also applies to newly discovered work and result delivery.
